title: Impulse and change in momentum
prereq: PH02 net force and time interval; PH01 signed velocity.
goals: Compute impulse as signed area under a net F–t graph.
Distinguish triangular peak force from average force.
Update final momentum and velocity through reversal or stopping.

sections.heading: Net impulse changes momentum
sections.body: The impulse–momentum law is Δp = J_net. With constant force, J = F_net Δt. With a changing net force, take the signed area of the force-versus-time graph. A positive region points right; a negative region contributes a leftward impulse.

sections.heading: A triangle is not a rectangle
sections.body: A triangular pulse of base Δt and peak F has signed area J = ½F_peak Δt. The peak is not the average force. For a triangle rising linearly from zero and returning to zero, the average is half the peak.

sections.heading: Add every segment
sections.body: If a positive pulse is followed by a negative interval, add both impulses with their signs. For a constant-mass body the velocity changes by J_net/m; use its INITIAL signed velocity and do not infer final direction from the initial arrow.

sections.heading: Which force was measured?
sections.body: The impulse–momentum theorem needs NET external force on the chosen body, not just one convenient contact force if friction, tension or another horizontal force acts during the interval.

worked.name: Foundation · brake without reversal
worked.setup: A 0.5 kg glider at +6 m/s experiences −10 N net force for 0.20 s.
worked.check: Negative impulse slowed motion; it did not reverse it.

worked.name: Connected · positive triangle
worked.setup: A triangular net force peaks at +20 N over 0.4 s on a 2 kg glider initially moving at −1 m/s.
worked.check: The triangular impulse is 4, not 8 N·s.

worked.name: Transfer · two pulses
worked.setup: A particle experiences successive impulses +12 N·s then −5 N·s.
steps: Without initial p and mass the final velocity is not uniquely determined.
worked.check: A correct impulse ledger does not invent missing initial conditions.

trap.wrong: Use F_peak Δt for a triangular pulse or ignore the area below the time axis.
trap.repair: Calculate each segment's area by shape and sign, then apply p_final = p_initial + ΣJ.

assumptions: Read the vertical axis as NET horizontal force.
Use consistent N, s, kg and m/s.
Only convert Δp to Δv using a constant mass.

model.label: Teaching model: triangular net-force peak over 0.4 s

prompt.stem: A 2 kg cart initially moves LEFT at −1 m/s. A NET force-time graph contains a +6 N triangular pulse from t=0 to 4 s, followed by a −4 N rectangular segment from t=4 to 5 s. Determine total signed impulse and final signed velocity.
prompt.prediction: Will the cart finish moving right, left or at rest after both signed areas?
prompt.boundaryPrompt: Halve the positive triangle's duration to 2 s but retain its +6 N peak; leave the −4 N for 1 s rectangle unchanged. Compute the new impulse and final velocity.
